v_cross: Crossword style: give a short English definition clue (like on the mock test: "reserve a holiday" = book, "untidy appearance" = scruffy, "holiday at sea" = cruise, "back of the foot" = heel, "warm woollen top" = jumper, "very thin (person)" = skinny). kind "type", hint = first letter + underscores + (number of letters). Topics: appearance, body, clothes, personality, travel, holidays, accommodation.
v_opp: Opposites with prefixes or a different word (honest, patient, responsible, tight clothes, mature, polite, considerate, reliable, secure, tidy, obedient, rational, tolerant, helpful, cheerful, generous, modest, sensitive, legal, loyal ...). q like "What is the opposite? HONEST". kind "type".
v_word: Complete with one word; the meaning is explained in brackets, exactly like the mock test ("After hiking all day, Jake looked like skin and ___. (extremely thin)", "We stayed in a ___ cottage where cold air came through the windows. (letting in cold air)" = draughty, "The hostel was popular with young ___ (budget travellers with rucksacks)" = backpackers, "We chose a self-___ apartment (providing cooking facilities)" = catering, "It is ___ to book early (practical and wise)" = sensible). kind "type", hint = first letter. Hard vocabulary from appearance, personality, travel.
v_conf: Words often confused, choose the correct word: trip/journey/travel/voyage, view/sight/outlook, ruins/wrecks/remnants, delay/postponement/interruption, companion/colleague/partner, brochures/leaflets/pamphlets, resort/destination, lay/lie, rise/raise, fun/funny. kind "choice" with 3 options.
v_prep: Prepositions in travel and holiday phrases and adjective+preposition collocations from the handout: by car, on foot, on the road, head for, on the coast, off the beaten track, on the move, in the heart of, arrive in/at, in a rush, famous for, familiar with, enthusiastic about, experienced in, expert on, eager for, put effort into, emphasis on, date back to, situated in, ideal for, open to, appeal to, be transformed into. kind "type".
v_phr: Phrasal verbs for journeys: set off, see off, hold up, get off, check in, check out, take off, break down, pick up, slow down, head for, get going, pass through, thumb a lift. Gap is the particle or the whole phrasal verb in correct form. kind "type".
v_idiom: Idioms from the handouts: not a hair out of place, down at heel, dressed to kill, look like a million dollars, all skin and bone, stand on your own two feet, get cold feet, lose your head, put ideas into someone's head, off the top of my head, give someone the cold shoulder, see eye to eye, keep your fingers crossed, pull someone's leg, keep a straight face, get something off your chest, raise a few eyebrows, on the tip of my tongue, have a change of heart, know something like the back of your hand, live out of a suitcase, put your feet up, get a move on, under the weather, in the nick of time, travel broadens the mind, hit the road, off the beaten track, travel light. Either choose the meaning or complete the missing word. Mix "choice" and "type".
v_form: Word formation exactly like the "Places to visit" handout: the base word in brackets must be changed (enjoy -> enjoyable, spice -> spicy, live -> lively, colour -> colourful, tradition -> traditional, peace -> peaceful, impress -> impressive, mountain -> mountainous, sand -> sandy, taste -> tasty/tasteful, luxury -> luxurious, space -> spacious, welcome -> welcoming, pollute -> unpolluted, end -> endless, bottom -> bottomless, comfort -> uncomfortable, price -> overpriced, cloud -> cloudless). q contains the base word in CAPITALS in brackets. kind "type".
v_clothes: Clothes, materials and patterns: translate from Slovene to English (plašč = coat, zimski plašč = overcoat, bluza = blouse, pulover = jumper/sweater, ovratnik = collar, rokavice s palcem = mittens, zadrga = zip, japonke = flip-flops, hlače = trousers, brezrokavnik = vest/waistcoat, jopica = cardigan, kopalni plašč = dressing gown/bathrobe, trenirka = tracksuit, bombaž = cotton, volna = wool, lan = linen, svila = silk, usnje = leather, semiš = suede, krzno = fur, črtast = striped, karirast = checked, cvetlični = floral, pikčast = spotted/polka-dot) and describe style (baggy, flared, knee-length, platform, collarless, scruffy, smart casual, worn-out). Mix "type" (Slovene prompt, English answer) and "choice".
v_appear: Appearance and personality descriptions: face shapes (round, oval, pointed), hair (receding, stubble, ginger, coarse, sleek, shoulder-length), build (plump, slim, skinny, stocky, well-built, overweight, underweight), complexion, freckles, wrinkles, middle-aged, in her forties, good-looking vs handsome vs beautiful, hair vs hairs; personality adjectives in context (nosy, childish, pessimistic, tactless, generous, impatient, pushy, fussy, diligent, down-to-earth, affectionate, pretentious, assertive, moody, reliable, considerate, stubborn). kind mostly "type" with hint first letter, some "choice".
v_holiday: Accommodation and holiday types: B&B, half board, full board, self-catering, all-inclusive, en-suite, single/twin/double room, package holiday, cruise, city break, camper van, campsite, hostel, guest house, resort; travel nouns: aisle seat, boarding card, travel insurance, foreign currency, tour operator, travel agency, departure lounge, jet lag, stopover, excursion, flying visit, globetrotter, pilgrim, backpacker, sightseer, rambler, explorer. Mix "choice" and "type".
v_odd: Worksheet task "Cross out the word that does not fit": a noun with four adjectives/collocates where exactly one does not collocate (e.g. sea: calm, rough, open, dark? -> choose the one that does NOT fit naturally; hotel: seaside, luxurious, accommodation, family -> accommodation). q like "Which word does NOT go with SEA?" kind "choice" with 4 options.
v_noun: Worksheet task "Guess the noun which goes with the adjectives": "clean, sandy, dirty, secluded ___" = beach; "narrow, busy, winding, cobbled ___" = street; "luxury, family, five-star, Victorian ___" = hotel; "rocky, snow-capped ___" = mountain(s); "trendy, expensive, second-hand, souvenir ___" = shop; "delicious, local, gourmet ___" = cuisine/food; "spectacular, breathtaking ___" = scenery/view. kind "type".
v_reply: Worksheet task "Match the sentences with a suitable reply": give a travel-related sentence and 3 possible replies; only one fits naturally and uses travel vocabulary (globetrotter, off the beaten track, travel light, thumb a lift, live out of a suitcase, all-inclusive, culture shock, B&B around the corner). kind "choice".
v_announce: Worksheet task "Read the announcements and underline the correct word" and similar transport/airport/hotel vocabulary in context: passengers/customers, platform/station, luggage/handbag, docking/landing, route/road, gate, boarding, check-in, departure lounge, jet lag, delay, detour, puncture, runway, cockpit, steward, ticket inspector, taxi rank. kind "choice" with 2 or 3 options.
p_dialog: Present Simple or Continuous inside a short two-person dialogue or phone conversation, exactly like handout EX. 4 (Ted and his dad): q contains "A: ... B: ..." with one gap and the verb in brackets, including negatives, questions and always+continuous. "a" lists all acceptable forms with contractions. kind "type". Hard.
v_explain_idiom: Explain-the-idiom or explain-the-phrasal-verb tasks from the handouts turned into multiple choice: q is a sentence using the idiom or phrasal verb, options are 3 meanings in English, exactly one correct. Use: not a hair out of place, down at heel, dressed to kill, put ideas into someone's head, off the top of my head, raise a few eyebrows, get something off your chest, keep a straight face, make up your mind, have a change of heart, see somebody off, hold up, set off, thumb a lift, live out of a suitcase, lose your nerve/heart, travel broadens the mind, make your way. kind "choice".
p_brackets: Mock test task "Use verbs in the correct form of Present Simple or Present Continuous": sentence with the verb in brackets, sometimes with subject or negation inside the brackets like "(he, be)", "(not, look)", "(you, want)", "(always, ask)", including questions, negatives, always+continuous complaints, timetables, fixed arrangements, temporary situations, and especially STATE vs DYNAMIC uses of see, think, have, expect, weigh, look, be, represent, appear, admire, taste, smell, feel, fit, mean, depend. q shows the brackets right after the gap. "a" must contain every acceptable form including contractions (e.g. "is having", "'s having"). kind "type". Make at least half of them tricky.
p_spell: Write the third person singular or the -ing form (wait, complete, enjoy, forget, happen, miss, say, try, fetch, fix, lie, make, begin, hop, hope, panic, travel, die, refer, visit, swim, admit, tie, carry, buy, play, wash, go, do). q like "Write the -ing form: hop". kind "type".
p_state: State verb or dynamic? Choose the correct form in pairs exactly like handout EX. 3 (SEE, THINK, ADMIRE, APPEAR, HAVE, EXPECT, WEIGH, LOOK, BE, REPRESENT): "A: How much ___ you ___? B: About 70 kilos." type tasks given as kind "choice" with 2 to 3 full options.
a_test: Mock test task "Complete with A / AN / THE or X (no article)". Cover: abstract nouns (crime, unemployment), institutions used for their purpose vs as buildings (in prison / to the prison, school, hospital, church, university), the + adjective groups (the poor, the rich, the elderly), sports (athletics), titles with names (President Trump, Queen Elizabeth), countries (the United States, the UK, the Netherlands vs France), rivers (the Thames), deserts (the Sahara), seas and oceans (the Mediterranean, the Pacific Ocean), lakes (Lake Geneva), mountain ranges (the Rocky Mountains) vs single mountains (Mount Everest), islands, illnesses (flu / the flu, a cold, a headache), meals, musical instruments (play the piano), unique things (the sun), first mention vs second mention, a/an by sound (an hour, a university, an MP, a European). options always exactly ["a","an","the","– (no article)"]; "correct" is the index. When both no article and the are accepted by grammar books, avoid the item.
